shrink to fit settings tab in admin dashboard on mobile also when clicking 
Maintenance Mode (Hide site from public) it should have a curtain closing the homepage displaying the company logo and stating under maintenance

**Adjusting Mobile Layout**

I'm currently focused on the mobile presentation of the Admin Dashboard's Settings tab. My main priority is reducing the space the settings occupy, especially considering the hidden sidebar. I'm exploring layout alternatives to ensure efficient information density on smaller screens. The user's feedback about the sidebar's potential space consumption is a key factor in my approach.


**Implement Mobile Navigation**

I've realized the Settings tab on mobile needs a dedicated navigation system. Right now, the hidden sidebar makes tab switching impossible on small screens. I'm focusing on adding a mobile-friendly tab navigation at the top, like a dropdown or horizontal list. My approach involves looking at `pages/admin/SettingsManager.tsx` to implement this. I also need to ensure the content itself is responsive on smaller devices.


**Crafting the Intro Animation**

I'm now diving into the specific CSS needed for the curtain animation. I'll utilize or adapt existing `curtain-down` keyframes defined in my project's `tailwind.config`. The plan is to modify `components/MaintenancePage.tsx` to implement a top-down or theater-style curtain effect. I'm focusing on the visual flow, making sure the logo and text reveal smoothly once the "curtain" opens. The `curtain-down` transform is a good starting point for a top-down drop.


**Adding Mobile Tab Selector**

I'm now prioritizing mobile-specific tab navigation. The existing tabs are hidden on smaller screens, a usability issue I need to address. I'll add a mobile-friendly tab selector above the content, using a `<select>` or a horizontally scrollable list of buttons.  This will make navigating the Settings section much easier on mobile devices.


**Revising Curtain Animation**

I've decided to refine the `curtain-down` animation in `MaintenancePage.tsx` using the pre-existing `curtain-down` keyframes. My focus is on making it look like a smooth, top-to-bottom drop. I'll make sure a container uses this class, creating a theater-style curtain effect.

\n\n**Addressing Settings Tab Navigation**

My latest focus has shifted towards the Settings tab's mobile presentation. To address the "shrink to fit" request, I am adding a mobile navigation selector, like a dropdown or horizontal scroll list, in `pages/admin/SettingsManager.tsx`. Also, I'm verifying all inputs have `w-full` for responsive width and proper padding. I'm ensuring grid layouts stack correctly on smaller screens.


**Designing Curtain Animation**

I'm now focusing on implementing the curtain animation on the maintenance page. I'm centering the logo and text on top of the curtain. I've re-reviewed the `curtain-down` keyframes defined in `index.html`. My aim is to use the `transform: translateY(-100%)` to create a smooth, top-to-bottom curtain reveal. I'll utilize a container with the relevant classes in `components/MaintenancePage.tsx` to get the theatrical effect I'm going for.


**Fine-tuning Settings Display**

I'm now zeroing in on the Settings tab within `pages/admin/SettingsManager.tsx`. I'm shrinking the padding and text sizes on mobile to address the "shrink to fit" request. The goal is to maximize visible content without sacrificing readability. The layout is `flex flex-col h-[calc(100vh-120px)]`, which makes it vertically scrollable, which is my goal. I'm also ensuring all input fields use `w-full` for responsiveness. I'm confident these adjustments will optimize the mobile experience.


**Defining Maintenance Page Style**

I'm now thinking about the visual impact of the maintenance page. I've realized the curtain animation is more of an entry effect than a "closing" animation, since it slides down on load for visitors. I'm focusing on making the color scheme immediately convey a sense of "maintenance". Instead of the default theme, I will use `bg-brand-green`, a solid color for the curtain's opaque appearance. I'll maintain the `bg-brand-dark` theme for the background for the sake of consistency.


**Finalizing Maintenance Animation**

My current focus is on the final touches of the maintenance page's animation. I'm ensuring the curtain transition uses the `curtain-down` keyframes defined in `tailwind.config`, making it appear as a top-to-bottom drop. In `components/MaintenancePage.tsx`, I'm utilizing `bg-brand-light` for high-contrast with light text for a "closed" feeling, and I will be using `opacity-0` with `animate-fade-in-delayed` classes to implement the fade in effect once the curtain has opened. I believe this will deliver the intended impact.


**Optimizing Mobile Layout**

I'm now implementing the mobile navigation, specifically targeting `pages/admin/SettingsManager.tsx`. I'll introduce a dropdown or horizontally scrollable list above the content. I'll test it out and ensure this new tab selector improves usability on smaller screens. Additionally, I am focused on maximizing content by adjusting the padding and using `w-full` for responsive width on inputs and grid layouts, so everything is clean and properly displayed.

This response updates the `SettingsManager` to be mobile-responsive with a dropdown navigation and tighter spacing ("shrink to fit"). It also revamps the `MaintenancePage` to include a dramatic curtain-closing animation with the company logo as requested.

entries.description: Added mobile tab navigation (dropdown), reduced padding for mobile ("shrink to fit"), and optimized layout density.
Implemented a full-screen theater curtain closing animation with company branding overlay.
